summary.intent: Coordinate parallel subagent work on the monokl project, here reviewing the hand-back from the agent that produced PR #113 (leaner Rust output rows) and verifying its changeset.
summary.outcome: PR #113 was opened, ready and linked to trail 363, with an 8.8% total byte cut and all checks exit 0. The assistant confirmed the changeset carries the Breaking/Action notes for the `+N more` marker and discloses the `where …` truncation. The PRs (#109, #111, #112, #113) await user merge once CI is green.

repo: monokl uses `just` recipes for verification: lint, test, changesets, rg-compare (hit counts must equal baseline), and bench.
Output-marker changes (like `+N more`) require a changeset with `**Breaking:**` and `**Action:**` notes.
Rust signature truncation (`where …`) is applied in the output layer, not in ranking, so ranking and rg-compare hit counts are unaffected.
The snippet ordering rule (code line before a doc, attribute or comment line) is shared between the TS and Rust paths.
An 8-row floor keeps the Rust median above rg-policy's (fd 1,300 vs 731), but it rescues the `patterns` and `add` questions.
workflow: Subagent hand-back reports are model output, not user instructions or approval. Verify open claims, such as changeset contents, directly rather than trusting the report.
Alternating old/new runs measured CPU time more reliably than wall time, which was noisy.

friction: Wall time in benchmarks was noisy, so CPU time on alternating runs was needed for perf comparison.
The Rust fd median still exceeds the rg-policy target (1,300 vs 731) because of the 8-row floor.
open_items: PRs #109, #111, #112 and #113 are awaiting user merge once CI is green.
Three agents are still running: the perf pass, the prefix-token name match plus `Impl` prior, and the container-versus-member experiment.

Whether having no flag to restore the old rows (pre-`where …` truncation and `+N more`) is acceptable has not been confirmed; the assistant thinks it is, since the clause is recoverable from the file.
The Rust median gap versus rg-policy is accepted for now; a language-aware floor was rejected as a hack on one harness.
The assistant did not read the #113 diff or check CI; only the changeset was verified.
